pairs.difference: A: the big pumpkin's contour is almost a plain dome, its ribs barely notch the outline, and it carries many thick spiral tendrils that end in rolled curls at left, right and top. Straight share is 0.084, well under the real range. B: the topiary is a stack of four tapering tiers on a flat-rimmed round plinth with a clear ring base. It is also low on straight share (0.185), but only because it is foliage, and its parts relate sensibly. Weak call, since both are organic.
pairs.fix: Draw fewer vines: one or two thin, short tendrils, not fat spirals. Give each pumpkin deep ribs that dent the outer edge.

pairs.difference: A: the cooler has a straight-sided tub with planar faces and fairly tight rim corners. The lid corners are rounder, but the numbers are in range (straight 0.582). B: the lion's plinth has stepped, flat faces and crisp edges, and the body and paws are correctly proportioned. Neither card shows swelling or missing parts.

A: the bat's head and body merge into one fat ball that takes up most of the torso, with tiny stub feet and oversized ears, so it reads as a plush toy. The wing scallops are soft lobes. Straight share 0.122 is below and corner rate 6.575 above the real range. B: the envelope and photo stack keep straight edges, flat planes and tight corners (straight 0.663), with the photos fanning out as thin sheets.
pairs.fix: Draw a slim bat with a small narrow body, a head much smaller than the wings, thin wing bones and sharp points where the wing membrane meets each finger.

pairs.difference: B: the cauldron is a plump sphere with a thick sausage-like rim, chunky ring handles and three stubby feet, inflated evenly all round. A: the sneakers are also chunky at the sole, but the collar, toe spring and laces break the outline with distinct parts, and the two shoes overlap convincingly. All numbers are in range, so this is a soft read.
pairs.fix: Make the cauldron rim a narrow lip, the ring handles thin iron loops and the feet slim and tapered, with a slightly flattened belly.

pairs.difference: B: the candelabra has fat candle stubs on wide cups, a thick looping arm on each side and a heavy domed foot. The contour is a run of bulges (corner rate 7.282, straight 0.181, solidity 0.433, all outside the real range). A: the street lamp has a large glass head, but the post, the curved arm and the scroll are slim and the part relations are believable. Its solidity of 0.63 is at the low edge and corner rate 4.738 is just over the real range.
pairs.fix: Draw taller, slimmer candles, thin metal arms with straight runs, shallow cups and a low flat base.

pairs.difference: B: the house walls bow in at the waist and the roof lines sag, so nothing runs straight, and the tower melts into the main mass. The window surrounds are thick and soft. A: only the wreath was masked, so its numbers (corner rate 21.806, straight 0.043) describe the leaves, not the card. On the image, the door panels, frame and handle are straight and planar, with tight corners.
pairs.fix: Keep the walls straight and vertical, with crisp roof edges and a clear gap between the tower and the main house. Lean the shapes only slightly.

pairs.difference: A: the headstone is a thick slab with a big soft arched top and no shoulder, and its edges are swollen like a pillow. The face bulges and the contour runs in one smooth blob down to the grass. B: the slide keeps its parts: a curved trough, posts, a platform and a ladder with thin rails and evenly spaced rungs. The trough is broad but its rails stay thin, and thin share reaches 0.011.
pairs.fix: Draw a thin flat stone slab with a square-cut base, a shallower arched top with defined shoulders, and tight bevelled edges on a flat face.

pairs.difference: A: the orb is enormous against a low stand, and the legs end in bulbous scroll blobs, which gives a toy top-heavy ratio. The stand's thin parts do survive, though. B: the vending machine is a true box with planar sides, straight runs (0.788), tight top corners and small feet, and its door, window and tray are correctly placed.
pairs.fix: Make the orb smaller, on a taller and more slender stand with thin legs that end in small neat feet.

pairs.difference: B: the broom head is built from a few fat tapered clumps like flame or leaf shapes, not fine straw, and the handle is a uniform tube with a rounded end. A: the mower has thin tubular handle bars with a real bend, wheels at the right scale and a stepped deck, though the deck is somewhat domed. Its solidity of 0.557 is low because of the open handle.
pairs.fix: Draw the broom head as many thin straight straws with a flat cut hem, and a slimmer handle that tapers.

pairs.difference: A: the coffin has flat faces, but its hexagon shoulders and foot are blunted so far that the contour has no measurable corners (corner rate 0.0, solidity 0.988, straight 0.752, all outside the real range). It is also wide and squat. B: the rocking chair is fully articulated, with slats, arms, spindles, a stretcher and rockers, and negative gaps between all of them. Only the cushion is puffy.
pairs.fix: Draw a long narrow coffin with sharp angled shoulders, crisp straight edges and a distinct lid overhang.

pairs.difference: A: the pumpkin outline is a nearly plain circle. The ribs barely notch the edge and the stem is a thick short curl. B: the jacket has puffy sleeves and sausage cuffs, but the collar, shoulder and hem still give a varied contour. Both are in range and both are inflated, so this is a slight lean only.
pairs.fix: Give the pumpkin deep ribs that scallop the outer edge, a slightly squat shape, and a narrower, angular cut stem.

pairs.difference: B: this coral copies the layout of the real coral in the reference sheet, but its arms are thicker fat fingers with bulbous tips and more even widths, and the rocks flatten into a single base mass (straight 0.097, corner rate 6.945, both outside the real range). A: the towel is a simple flat rectangle with gently wavy edges. Its low corner rate (0.366) suits soft cloth, and its proportions are right.
pairs.fix: Thin the coral arms so they taper to narrower tips and vary in width, and keep each rock as a separate faceted stone.

pattern: Generated cards inflate forms evenly. Rims, feet, handles and cuffs thicken into tubes, thin parts lose width, slabs get blunted shoulders, and walls or edges bow where real cards keep straight runs and tight corners. On silhouette, generated objects are also often squatter or top-heavy, with a big main mass on undersized supports, as with the bat, orb and headstone. The lessons show this drift is subtle on the best variants, so several calls here are low confidence. Caveat: the run path says "horror", and most pairs contain one spooky object, which nudged my low-confidence picks (p04, p09, p11). Those three are only weakly supported by shape alone. The p06 wreath numbers are a mask artefact and should be ignored.
